description: An open-source bastion host (jump server) for SSH, RDP, VNC and Telnet with web access, session recording, audit logs and Casdoor SSO

latest_release.body:
## Changelog
### Features
* d1dc50134ec1b55ccd63f070c2ce9482c6dc2438 feat: add Desktop assets to control computers running Casvisor Desktop from the browser
* e5cd4c707bf3c7e2a7f27ce0da3c91967c1fff77 feat: add Kubernetes assets to open a shell in a container from the browser, with command rules, recording and live monitoring
* c635560ccad248e518ac16a9118c40b728b69269 feat: add a Prometheus metrics endpoint protected by a bearer token
* dee2d17e7ac40494faf7292dc422f498eb7f67af feat: add an asset tree whose nodes can be granted in permissions, and import and export assets as CSV
* e8ba4b5f59647aeb821b1e540ad2795ea23b7cd8 feat: add login rules that allow, reject, hold for review or require two-step verification by user, IP and time, on the web and the SSH gateway
* b92c085ec7f823fc413f34382442d21250696ea2 feat: let administrators take control of a live terminal session from the monitor, with their commands logged as the operator
* a07cfc64420242d9b196c7ad5810cac58621de96 feat: limit permissions to weekdays and hours of the day, disconnecting sessions when the hours end
* 2056ca1688bc97db9e737f170e47f3673529cd74 feat: notify DingTalk, Feishu, WeCom, Slack or any URL of blocked commands, access requests and sign-in reviews through webhooks
* 45d7d3876c66418ad3d0cd324e488e1ad58e4d9c feat: open the same asset in more than one workbench tab and jump from a command to its moment in the replay
* 21e9e6e64596aa0ce94b85d5cab88497e95b9caf feat: show a watermark with the user, client IP and time over the sessions a permission covers
* a7aa5079ea829e658b1bac8d07ad0d80de8f2a61 feat: sign in to the SSH gateway with OpenSSH certificates from a trusted CA
* 1201ac9f3abee1fe6e2fb7facabbf60092f4eb3c feat: store session recordings in S3-compatible object storage, uploading them when sessions end and retrying when the bucket is down
* 2e8ae0f1716c055d1bce3c2c357023321467fd6d feat: test the connection to an asset from its edit page before saving it
### Bug fixes
* 5725303dc3b4382a846f9b5fb3a12c67da48ebd3 fix: check every owner in a request, sign out other sessions on password change and re-read Casdoor users of connected sessions
* d44c5c0300773d2e81e44288606f4e5290ef48e1 fix: check request origins, trusted proxies, one connection per session, Ctrl+J and pasted lines in command rules, and secrets kept on edited assets
* 39c43fc555459f62a9c963f3e735fc9da55f3cc4 fix: encrypt credentials by default with a key file next to the SQLite database, and encrypt the credentials of all tables at startup
* c92b08ec7b6e27ccb65f88839be51cc427e0c6ac fix: keep organization admins within their own organization and make audit records append-only
* 5339402bc66ad9842de98b11c5df7517bdbc720d fix: keep the server up on bad terminal escape sequences, huge terminal sizes, gzip bodies and asset names with two slashes
* bdc5ea630dd97516f307e44d717aa1583eaf7a8f fix: keep the sign-in with Casvisor's own accounts in production builds of the frontend
* 8fa1c0dadf2ba3123be6ced9d37e772c3f81e54a fix: let only one reviewer change an access request, accept each TOTP code once, block commands when the rules can't be read, and escape database exports
* e5b2a5ff2772fe589bd351d14a0d93f15924960a fix: run golangci-lint v2 in CI so that it can read go 1.25 modules
* 5fe321150a98d70da35f4f7650b79e30bd54197a fix: send Ctrl+Alt+Delete to Desktop assets as a control message
* e88e07c0636ba2b5abf9ca7385c5e4c126af13f2 fix: send typed connect credentials in the tunnel request body instead of WebSocket URLs, and stop keeping them in localStorage
* 7f82ea7888217600fa3f6eccfb31c740ecded18f fix: serve static files only from inside web/build
* 8cbf25f69ce7a9fc6e97bea3dbd005a695129a7c fix: sort the unpaginated session list by created_time
* c8c05da57569a90ab1bc859d647a18846b0379af fix: update golang.org/x/crypto, x/net, gorilla/websocket, pgx and golang-jwt

detail.readme:
An open-source bastion host (jump server) for SSH, RDP, VNC, Telnet and databases

Casvisor gives your team one place to reach servers, desktops and databases from the browser.
It connects over SSH, RDP, VNC, Telnet, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Redis, MongoDB and HTTP for internal websites, with an SSH gateway for ssh, scp and VS Code,
and records every session, checks every command and keeps the passwords to itself.

Website · Documentation · Live demo · Discord

SSH and VNC in the browser, with rm -rf / stopped by a command rule and every command on record.

Session replay. Play back SSH, Telnet, VNC and RDP sessions in the browser, with the commands beside them. Command records. Every command and SQL statement, and which rule blocked or flagged it. Permissions. Who can reach which assets, from where, until when and with which actions.
## 🚀 Try it in 30 seconds No database and no config file needed. This runs Casvisor on SQLite with its own accounts: ```bash docker run -d --name casvisor -p 19000:19000 -p 2222:2222 \ -v casvisor-db:/db -v casvisor-recordings:/recordings casbin/casvisor docker logs casvisor ``` Open and sign in: | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Username | `admin` | | Password | the one printed in `docker logs casvisor` | > Pass `-e adminPassword=` to choose the first password instead. Either way, change it under **My Account** after you sign in. Prefer not to install anything? The hosted demo at **[demo.casvisor.com](https://demo.casvisor.com)** comes with a sandboxed Linux shell (SSH) and a private desktop (VNC) to connect to. Nothing there touches a real server, sessions end after 15 minutes, and each visitor can keep two sessions open at a time. ## 🤔 Why Casvisor Casvisor sits between the people who run your servers and the servers themselves. People open sessions from a browser tab, or with their own `ssh`, `scp` and VS Code through the SSH gateway. They only reach the servers and databases a permission gives them, and never see the stored passwords. - **One Go binary.** Casvisor speaks SSH, RDP, VNC, Telnet, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Redis, MongoDB and HTTP itself, with nothing to install on the servers. It runs on SQLite with its own accounts out of the box. - **Apache-2.0, no enterprise edition.** Recording, the SSH gateway, network gateways, system accounts, jobs and everything else in this README are in the open-source project. - **Policy you can read.** Permissions are enforced with [Casbin](https://casbin.apache.org), and sign-in can be handed to [Casdoor](https://casdoor.ai) for SSO, MFA, LDAP and social logins. - **Audit by default.** Sessions are recorded, commands and SQL statements are checked against your rules and logged, and the logs export to CSV or a syslog server. Coming from another bastion host? See how Casvisor [compares with JumpServer, Teleport and others](https://casvisor.org/docs/more/comparison). ## 📦 Installation Three supported paths, fastest first. All of them end up at . ### Docker ```bash docker run -d --name casvisor -p 19000:19000 -p 2222:2222 \ -v casvisor-db:/db -v casvisor-recordings:/recordings casbin/casvisor ``` Port 19000 is the web console and port 2222 is the SSH gateway. The two volumes keep the database and the session recordings when the container is replaced. Guide: [Quick start](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/quickstart) ### Docker Compose [`docker-compose.yml`](docker-compose.yml) builds the image from this repository and runs it with the same ports and volumes: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` Set `adminPassword` in the compose file to choose the first password of `admin`; when it is empty, a random one is printed in the log. ### From source — for development Use this if you intend to modify Casvisor. Prerequisites: **Go 1.23+** (see [`go.mod`](go.mod)), **Node.js 20 LTS** and **Yarn 1.x**. ```bash git clone https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor cd casvisor/web && yarn install && yarn build && cd .. go run main.go ``` Guide: [Build from source](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/source) ### Configuration Settings are read from [`conf/app.conf`](conf/app.conf). Put the settings of your own server in `conf/app.local.conf` (same format, not tracked by git), or pass any of them as environment variables. **Database.** The default is SQLite. To use MySQL instead (the database is created if it does not exist): ```ini driverName = mysql dataSourceName = root:123456@tcp(localhost:3306)/ dbName = casvisor ``` **Sign in with Casdoor.** Instead of its own accounts, Casvisor can sign users in with [Casdoor](https://casdoor.ai), for SSO, MFA, LDAP and third-party logins, and use Casdoor's groups in permissions. Create an organization and an application for Casvisor in Casdoor, add `http:///callback` to the redirect URLs of the application, and set: ```ini casdoorEndpoint = https:// clientId = clientSecret = casdoorOrganization = casdoorApplication = ``` When `casdoorEndpoint` is empty, Casvisor uses its own accounts. **Recordings.** Sessions are recorded to `recordings/` under the working directory (`/recordings` in Docker). `recordingPath` moves them, `recordingRetentionDays` deletes the ones older than that many days, and `disableRecording = true` turns recording off. To keep them in an S3-compatible bucket instead, set: ```ini recordingStorage = s3 recordingS3Endpoint = s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com recordingS3Region = us-east-1 recordingS3Bucket = recordingS3Prefix = casvisor recordingS3AccessKey = recordingS3SecretKey = ``` Recordings are still written to the disk first, so a session never waits for the bucket; when the session ends the recording is uploaded and the local copy deleted (`recordingKeepLocal = true` keeps it). If the bucket can't be reached, the upload is retried every 5 minutes. `recordingS3PathStyle = true` is for MinIO and others that need path-style URLs. **SSH certificates.** To let users sign in to the SSH gateway with OpenSSH certificates instead of registering public keys, set `sshGatewayTrustedUserCaKeys` to the CA public keys (one per line or separated by `;`) or to a file of them, like sshd's `TrustedUserCAKeys`. The certificate's principal is the Casvisor user, `` or `/`; validity, `source-address` and the login rules are checked. **Metrics.** Set `metricsToken` and point Prometheus at `/metrics` with `authorization: {credentials: }`. It is off while `metricsToken` is empty. Guide: [Configuration](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/configuration) · [Sign in with Casdoor](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/casdoor) · [Behind a reverse proxy](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/reverse-proxy) ## 👉 After you sign in At this point you have a running bastion host with nothing behind it yet. Next: 1. **Change the `admin` password** under **My Account**, and turn on two-step verification there. 2. **[Add an asset](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/assets)** under **Assets** (a server, a desktop or a database) and click **Connect**. Administrators reach every asset. 3. **[Let other people in](https://casvisor.org/docs/access-control/permissions)**: add them under **Users** and give them a **Permission** on assets or asset tags. 4. **[Use the SSH gateway](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/ssh-gateway)**: users add their public key under **SSH keys** and connect with `ssh -p 2222 @`. 5. **[Add command rules](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/commands)** to block or flag commands such as `rm -rf /` or `DROP DATABASE`. ## ✨ Features **🔌 Connect** - **SSH** — an xterm.js terminal in the browser, with a file panel beside it for upload and download over SFTP - **RDP** — [gordp](https://github.com/casvisor/gordp), a pure-Go RDP client: NLA, the GFX graphics pipeline (ClearCodec, RemoteFX Progressive) like the Windows client, sharp text on high-DPI screens, the remote cursor, clipboard with text, images and files, resizing with the window, and file transfer through a redirected drive. Works with Windows Server, Windows 10/11 and FreeRDP-based hosts such as Ubuntu - **VNC** — noVNC in the browser; Casvisor does the VNC authentication itself, so the password stays on the server - **Telnet** — for network gear and old systems, logging in with the asset's account - **MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server and Oracle** — a browser SQL console with the databases, tables and columns on the left, one tab per result, and CSV export; SQL Server scripts run batch by batch between `GO` lines, and Oracle PL/SQL blocks end with a `/` line - **Redis and MongoDB** — the same console for Redis commands, with the keys and their types on the left, and for MongoDB shell calls such as `db.users.find({age: {$gt: 18}}).sort({name: 1})`, with the collections and their fields on the left - **Websites** — internal web apps such as Grafana, Jenkins or a router's admin page, each opened on a subdomain of its own through Casvisor's reverse proxy, WebSockets included, with optional HTTP basic authentication filled in by Casvisor; uploads and downloads follow the `Upload` and `Download` actions, and pages opened and changing requests are recorded - **SSH gateway** — `ssh -p 2222 web-01@casvisor.example.com`, `scp`, `sftp`, `rsync`, Xshell and VS Code Remote, signed in with the user's public key, or an OpenSSH certificate from a CA you trust (Vault, step-ca, `ssh-keygen -s`), and under the same permissions as the browser; `-L` also forwards Unix sockets such as `/var/run/docker.sock` - **Port forwarding to any asset** — `ssh -p 2222 -N -L 13389:win-01:3389 alice@casvisor.example.com`, then mstsc, a VNC viewer or a database client connects to `localhost:13389` - **Network gateways** — reach assets in another data center or behind NAT, through an SSH jump host or an agent that connects out over HTTPS - **Stored credentials** — passwords and private keys are encrypted in the database and filled in by Casvisor; SSH host keys and RDP certificates are pinned on first use **🛡️ Control** - **Permissions** — on users, groups, assets and asset tags, with the actions `Connect`, `Copy`, `Paste`, `Upload`, `Download` and `Forward`, client IP ranges, a start and end date, and weekly hours such as Monday to Friday 09:00–18:00; open sessions are disconnected when the hours end - **System accounts** — several accounts per asset, such as `root`, `deploy` and `readonly`; permissions decide which one a user may connect with, and passwords can be changed by hand or on a schedule - **Access requests** — users ask for an asset with a reason and an end time, an administrator approves, and withdrawing it disconnects open sessions - **Two-step verification** — for local accounts, with any TOTP authenticator app - **Command rules** — block or flag commands matching a regular expression, in the web terminal, the SQL console, website requests and through the SSH gateway alike - **Revocation takes effect at once** — open sessions are disconnected as soon as their permission or account is edited, deleted or expires **🔍 Audit** - **Session recording and playback** — SSH, Telnet, VNC and RDP, replayed in the browser with the same code that drew them live; SSH and Telnet recordings download as asciicast. Recordings are kept on disk or moved to an S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Alibaba Cloud OSS, Tencent COS, Cloudflare R2, MinIO) when the session ends - **Live monitoring** — watch online sessions and stop any of them; an administrator can take part in a terminal session and type in it, the user is told who joined, and the commands are logged with the administrator as the operator - **Command records** — SSH and Telnet commands are read off a virtual screen, so tab completion, history and line edits are captured as they ran; SQL statements are logged too - **Operation log** — file transfers and every change made through the API - **Export and syslog** — session, command and operation logs export to CSV and can be forwarded to a syslog server as RFC 5424 JSON or CEF **⚙️ Operate** - **Jobs** — run a command, a Bash or PowerShell script, or a file copy on many SSH assets at once, with concurrency, timeouts and per-asset output and exit codes - **Patch management** — scan SSH assets for pending system updates, install them and restart, on Windows (Windows Update) and Linux (apt, dnf, yum) - **REST API** — every console action is also an API call, with [Swagger docs](swagger) - **Prometheus metrics** — `/metrics` reports connected sessions, sessions, commands, assets, access requests and network agents, behind the bearer token in `metricsToken` - **Web console** — in 9 languages, built with React, Vite and shadcn/ui ## 🌐 Network gateways Assets in another data center, or behind NAT in an office, are reached through a network gateway. Add one under **Network gateways** and pick it in the asset's **Network gateway** field. Every connection to the asset (web SSH, Telnet, VNC, RDP, databases, the SSH gateway and patch management) then goes through it. - **SSH jump host**: a server in that network that Casvisor can log in to over SSH. Nothing is installed on it; its sshd needs `AllowTcpForwarding yes`. - **Agent**: for networks Casvisor cannot connect into at all. Generate a token on the gateway's page and run the agent on any machine in that network: ```bash casvisor agent --server https://casvisor.example.com --token cva_... --fingerprint SHA256:... ``` The agent is the same `casvisor` binary (with Docker: `docker run -d --restart unless-stopped casbin/casvisor agent --server ...`). It connects out to Casvisor's web address over WebSocket, so it works wherever HTTPS gets out, listens on no port, and only connects to the **Allowed networks** set on the gateway. Guide: [Network gateways](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/network-gateways) ## 🧱 Technology stack Casvisor is a frontend–backend separated application: - **Backend** — Go with the [Beego](https://github.com/beego/beego) framework: the REST API, the protocol tunnels and the SSH gateway ([repository root](https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor)) - **Frontend** — React with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) on Tailwind CSS, built with Vite: the console, the workbench and the session player ([`web/`](web)) - **RDP** — [casvisor/gordp](https://github.com/casvisor/gordp), a pure-Go RDP client - **Authorization** — [Casbin](https://casbin.apache.org) - **Database** — SQLite or MySQL through [XORM](https://xorm.io/) ## 📖 Documentation The full documentation lives at **[casvisor.org](https://casvisor.org/docs)**. Common starting points: | I want to… | Go to | |------------|-------| | Install Casvisor | [Quick start](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/quickstart) · [From source](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/source) | | Connect to servers and databases | [Protocols](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/protocols) · [Databases](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/databases) · [SSH gateway](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/ssh-gateway) | | Decide who can reach what | [Permissions](https://casvisor.org/docs/access-control/permissions) · [Access requests](https://casvisor.org/docs/access-control/access-requests) | | Review what people did | [Recordings](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/recordings) · [Commands](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/commands) · [Export](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/export) | | Run it in production | [Configuration](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/configuration) · [Reverse proxy](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/reverse-proxy) · [Upgrading](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/upgrading) | ## 🔒 Security **Please do not report security vulnerabilities in public GitHub issues.** Email instead. Before exposing a Casvisor instance to the internet: - Change the `admin` password and turn on two-step verification, or sign in through Casdoor. - Serve Casvisor over HTTPS only, behind a reverse proxy, and set `trustedProxies` and `allowedOrigins` in [`conf/app.conf`](conf/app.conf). - Keep port 2222 (the SSH gateway) closed to networks that do not need it. - Back up the credential key with the database: stored passwords and private keys cannot be decrypted without it. It is `credentialKey` in the config, or `credential.key` next to the SQLite database when that is not set. ## 🤝 Community and support - **Discord** — [join the community](https://discord.gg/yfKcuHVAHB) for questions and help - **GitHub Issues** — [bug reports and feature requests](https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor/issues) ## 🌍 Contributing Contributions are welcome. For anything larger than a small fix, **please open an issue first** so you can agree on the approach with the maintainers before writing code. **Translations.** User-facing strings in the web console go through [i18next](https://www.i18next.com/). After adding or changing one under [`web/`](web), run `go test -tags manual ./i18n -run TestGenerateI18nStrings` to add the new keys to every catalog in [`web/src/locales/`](web/src/locales), then translate them. ## 📄 License Casvisor is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). ---
